summary: A target-complete field-presentation follow-up of the accepted T.1 packet: the explicit commutator symbol, homogeneous two-sided Milnor quotient, tensor-square universal property, complete lifted toral relations and faithful coefficient extension give a specified Matsumoto equivalence with naturality. Infinite fields and finite fields have separate proof routes. Predecessor definitions retain their IDs; the graded Quillen comparison remains imported and its exact product-symbol supplier obligation is recorded. Inherited stable group and companion product proof refinements are explicit gaps, so coverage is planned rather than closed. Nothing is formalised.

nodes.title: Bilinear Steinberg pairings
nodes.statement: For an abelian group A written additively, IsSteinbergPairing(c) for c:Fˣ×Fˣ→A means c(ab,d)=c(a,d)+c(b,d), c(a,bd)=c(a,b)+c(a,d), and c(a,b)=0 whenever a+b=1 in F. The last condition uses the field values of two units, so neither zero nor a fake totalised inverse enters the definition.
hypotheses: F is a field and A is an AddCommGroup.
proofSteps: Use a predicate on an actual function with these three equations; do not put derived identities into the definition.
Convert each multiplicative variable to Additive Fˣ. Additive group homomorphisms are automatically ℤ-linear, supplying the tensor-product universal property.
Prove closure under postcomposition by additive homomorphisms and under pullback by field homomorphisms.
acceptance: The conclusion holds at the displayed maps, with the stated orientations and hypotheses.

nodes.title: Integral symbol identities
nodes.statement: Every Steinberg pairing satisfies c(a,-a)=0, c(a,b)=-c(b,a), c(a,a)=c(a,-1), and 2c(a,a)=0. In characteristic two c(a,a)=0. The assertion c(a,a)=0 is false for general integral coefficients.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: Bilinearity implies that the value at a unit 1 is zero and inversion negates either variable.
If a≠1, both 1-a and 1-a⁻¹ are units and -a=(1-a)/(1-a⁻¹). The two Steinberg relations show c(a,-a)=0. If a=1, use the unit-one equation. This covers F₂ without introducing 1/(1-a).
Expand c(ab,-ab)=0, splitting -ab once as (-a)b and once as a(-b); the terms c(a,-a) and c(b,-b) vanish, leaving c(a,b)+c(b,a)=0.
Expand c(a,-a)=c(a,-1)+c(a,a). Since 2c(a,-1)=c(a,(-1)²)=0, negating c(a,-1) has no effect. This gives the stated diagonal formula.
acceptance: No division by 1-a occurs in the a=1 branch.
The real sign pairing has c(-1,-1)=1, disproving integral alternation.
Characteristic-two diagonal vanishing is stated separately from skew-symmetry.

sources.match: Field specialization of the negative-unit argument; the a=1 case is supplied explicitly.

nodes.title: Universal degree-two symbol presentation
nodes.statement: Put U=Additive Fˣ and P₂(F)=(U⊗ℤU)/R₂, where R₂ is the ℤ-submodule spanned by a⊗b for unit pairs with a+b=1. Let p(a,b) be the quotient class of a⊗b. For every abelian A, evaluation on p gives a bijection between additive maps P₂(F)→A and Steinberg pairings Fˣ×Fˣ→A.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: Form the submodule on the indicated set of pure tensors, using the standard ℤ-module structures.
Lift a pairing by the tensor universal property. Its lift annihilates the generating tensors and therefore the entire span.
Descend with Submodule.liftQ. Conversely compose any additive homomorphism with the pure-tensor quotient to get a pairing.
Use generation by pure tensors and surjectivity of the quotient map to prove the two operations are inverse. No injectivity into classical K₂ is used here.
acceptance: The conclusion holds at the displayed maps, with the stated orientations and hypotheses.

nodes.title: Homogeneity of the two-sided Steinberg ideal
nodes.statement: In the predecessor’s tensor-algebra Milnor construction, let T=TensorAlgebra ℤ U, T_d its existing homogeneous pieces, and J the least two-sided ideal containing ι(a)ι(b) for a+b=1. Every homogeneous component of every z∈J lies in J. Moreover J∩T₀=J∩T₁=0, and J∩T₂ is exactly the ℤ-span of the Steinberg degree-two products.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: Use TwoSidedIdeal and its complete lattice: J is the intersection of all ideals containing the displayed products. The tensor algebra is noncommutative, so a left-ideal span alone is insufficient.
Identify J additively with finite sums of sandwiches z·ι(a)ι(b)·w. Closure under left/right multiplication proves this description has the required minimality.
Decompose z and w into their finite homogeneous sums using the existing direct-sum grading. Every resulting sandwich has degree deg(z)+2+deg(w). Group the finite sum by degree.
The component of each degree is again a sum of sandwiches, proving homogeneity. Nonnegative grading implies there are no terms of degree zero or one.
For degree two, the two outer degrees must both be zero. T₀ is ℤ, so these sandwiches are precisely the integer span of the Steinberg products. The converse containment is immediate.
acceptance: Use the existing TensorAlgebra.gradedAlgebra instance, not a new tensor grading.
Left and right multiplication by degree-one tensors preserve the ideal and raise the relation degree to three.
Degree-zero and degree-one embeddings into T/J are injective.

sources.match: Refinement of the homogeneous quotient claimed by the Milnor definition; the homogeneous-sandwich proof makes its two-sided nature explicit.

nodes.title: Milnor quotient grading and symbol API
nodes.statement: Refine the imported Milnor ring Kᴹ(F)=T/J by equipping it with the ℕ-grading whose degree-d piece is the image of T_d under the congruence quotient. The direct sum of these pieces maps isomorphically to Kᴹ(F). Define n-symbols as products of the imported degree-one unit classes; they generate degree n, are multilinear and vanish when consecutive entries sum to one.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: Apply the quotient ring to the ring congruence of J; this is a Ring, not a commutative-ring quotient of T.
Define each homogeneous image as an ℤ-submodule. Multiplication sends degree i times degree j to degree i+j since the quotient map is a ring homomorphism.

For injectivity of the direct-sum reconstruction, lift each summand to T_i. If their sum lies in J, homogeneity puts each lift in J, so every image summand vanishes. Surjectivity follows by decomposing an arbitrary representative.
Factor finite tensor words through the quotient. A consecutive Steinberg relation is a sandwich of a defining relation, which is zero.
Identify Kᴹ₀(F) with ℤ and Kᴹ₁(F) with U using the previously established vanishing intersections.
acceptance: The conclusion holds at the displayed maps, with the stated orientations and hypotheses.

nodes.title: Degree two equals the tensor-square presentation
nodes.statement: There is a canonical additive equivalence Kᴹ₂(F)≃P₂(F) taking the two-entry Milnor symbol {a,b} to p(a,b). This is an equivalence of the two specified quotient constructions; it is independent of classical or Quillen K-theory.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: Identify the degree-two tensor-algebra submodule with U⊗ℤU by extending (u,v)↦ι(u)ι(v).

Construct the inverse by projecting tensor words to degree two: length-two words go to their pure tensor; words of every other length go to zero. The multilinearity relations defining TensorAlgebra respect this projection.
Use J∩T₂=R₂ to descend both directions. Check the composites on degree-two products, then extend by their additive generation.
acceptance: The equivalence sends {1/2,1/2} to zero over ℚ.
Both maps are fixed on symbols; there is no arbitrary chosen isomorphism.

nodes.title: Functorial maps on the Milnor presentation
nodes.statement: For a field homomorphism f:F→E construct the graded ring map Kᴹ(f) induced by units a↦f(a). Its degree-two map corresponds under the tensor-square equivalences to p(a,b)↦p(f(a),f(b)); identity and composition are strict map equalities.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: A field homomorphism is injective and maps units to units. Its induced additive-unit map is ℤ-linear.
Lift to the tensor algebra. It sends each generating Steinberg product into the target Steinberg ideal because f(a)+f(b)=1. Hence it preserves J and descends to the quotient.
On n-symbols it sends every entry through f and preserves degree. Prove identity and composition on degree-one generators and use ring-hom extensionality.
acceptance: The conclusion holds at the displayed maps, with the stated orientations and hypotheses.

nodes.title: Field Weyl and diagonal lift calculus
nodes.statement: Use the predecessor’s w_ij(a)=x_ij(a)x_ji(-a⁻¹)x_ij(a) and h_ij(a)=w_ij(a)w_ij(-1). In St_n(F), n≥3, their conjugation on every root subgroup is the signed and rescaled matrix Weyl/torus action. In particular w_ij(a)⁻¹=w_ij(-a), h_ij(a)x_kl(t)h_ij(a)⁻¹=x_kl(d_k t d_l⁻¹), where d_i=a,d_j=a⁻¹ and all other d_k=1.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: Reuse the existing lift words; no new presentation of St_n is introduced.
For non-opposite roots expand the three factors of w and apply the three Steinberg relations, retaining all distinct-index hypotheses.

For opposite roots use a third index to express x_ij(t)=[x_ik(t),x_kj(1)]. Conjugate both factors by w, using the already checked non-opposite cases; this supplies the rank-one identities without assuming them as relations.
Compose the Weyl conjugations for w(a)w(-1) to obtain the diagonal rescaling. Read each elementary-image equation against the existing pinned transvection API.
acceptance: Rank two is excluded.
At a=-1 the elementary image of h is diag(-1,-1); it is not the identity over ℚ.
Disjoint root coordinates are fixed; adjacent parameters have the displayed scaling.

nodes.title: Diagonal commutator equals the toral defect
nodes.statement: In stable St(F), for distinct i,j,k and units a,b, the chosen classical symbol s(a,b)=[h_ij(a),h_ik(b)] equals c_ij(a,b)=h_ij(a)h_ij(b)h_ij(ab)⁻¹. The positive roots e_i-e_j and e_i-e_k have Cartan pairing +1. The corresponding simple adjacent roots instead have pairing -1; their toral commutator is c(a,b)⁻¹.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: Every defect c_ij(a,b) lies in the stable kernel, hence is central by the imported stable theorem.
The lift-calculus conjugation gives h_ik(b)h_ij(a)h_ik(b)⁻¹=h_ij(ab)h_ij(b)⁻¹. Therefore its inverse commutator is h_ij(a)h_ij(b)h_ij(ab)⁻¹, exactly s(a,b).

Transport between positive root pairs by signed permutation words built from w; their conjugations fix central kernel elements. This makes the common positive-root defect independent of i<j, with the reverse-root orientation handled separately.
For arbitrary roots use the Cartan exponent in [h_α(a),h_β(b)]=c_α(a,b^{⟨β,α∨⟩}). Fix both the +1 overlap and -1 adjacency cases; never switch between them silently.
acceptance: The normalization is the displayed commutator, not its inverse.
The matrix image of c_ij is 1, but that fact alone is not used to conclude c_ij=1.
The comparison agrees with Matsumoto’s cocycle for the +1 root overlap.

sources.match: The commutator/cocycle identity with its Cartan exponent; the direct stable calculation also works over finite fields.
Uses the explicit symbol convention; the inverse-defect mismatch in the exercise is recorded as source issue E-T2-2.

nodes.title: The explicit classical symbol is a pairing
nodes.statement: The predecessor’s symbol s:Fˣ×Fˣ→Additive K₂(F) is a Steinberg pairing. It is independent of stabilizing coordinates and is natural under field homomorphisms. This supplies the field case without appealing to the predecessor’s general-ring Whitehead conjugation gap.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: The elementary diagonals commute, so their lift commutator lies in K₂. Centrality gives independence of lifts.
For a product aa′ in either argument, replace h(aa′) by h(a)h(a′) times its central defect. The central factor disappears from the commutator; the commutator product law supplies bilinearity.
For a+b=1 expand w(a)w(-1)w(b). The identities a-a²=ab, b-b²=ab and a⁻¹+b⁻¹=(ab)⁻¹ reduce this word to w(ab), hence h(a)h(b)=h(ab). Cocycle normalization yields s(a,b)=0.
Coordinate changes use actual elementary signed permutation words, not arbitrary GL conjugation. Field homomorphisms preserve each of the three w factors and thus h and the commutator.
acceptance: The Steinberg relation has two unit inputs and does not assert a symbol at zero.
The case a=1 is addressed by pairing-identities, rather than a nonexistent unit 1-a.

sources.match: The complete word calculation for the Steinberg relation.
Bilinearity for type A and its relation to the bilinear symbol conditions.

nodes.title: Lifted Bruhat reduction and complete toral relations
nodes.statement: For n≥3 and any field F, quotient St_n(F) by the normal closure of the defects h_ij(a)h_ij(b)h_ij(ab)⁻¹. The map from this quotient to SL_n(F) is an isomorphism. In the quotient, Bruhat words reduce to u·h·w·v, with ordered positive-root products u,v, simple-coroot diagonal word h, and a chosen signed permutation representative w. An element mapping to the identity reduces to the identity; no uniqueness of both outer unipotent factors is claimed.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: Gaussian elimination over F identifies E_n(F) with SL_n(F); ordinary Bruhat decomposition and its Weyl combinatorics are imported from their upstream owners.
Order positive roots by increasing height. Steinberg commutator relations collect their products; inspection of triangular matrix entries proves the collected root-subgroup map injective.
Use the lift calculus to move diagonal and Weyl words across collected unipotent products. Modulo the defects, h_ij is multiplicative. Rewrite all diagonal words in the simple-coroot coordinates.

The union of the Bruhat word sets is stable under left multiplication by each generator: positive roots collect directly; simple Weyl generators split into the increasing/decreasing-length cases. For an opposite root with nonzero parameter use the three-factor w identity, whose torus parameter is its inverse.

If the matrix image is 1, ordinary Bruhat forces w=1; diagonal coordinates then force h=1. The remaining unipotent product is trivial by triangular injectivity. This proves injectivity of the quotient and completeness of the presentation, rather than merely checking its matrix relations.
acceptance: The result includes n=3 over F₂ and F₃; it does not assert universal centrality in that rank.
Injectivity is proved through the Bruhat reduction, not from faithfulness of an already defined matrix action.

sources.match: The complete Chevalley presentation specialized to A_{n-1}; ordinary Bruhat is imported, while the lift reduction is planned here.
Distinguishes the unique monomial component from non-unique outer factors; its infinite-field restriction is not used to extend this theorem to finite fields.

nodes.title: Symbols generate the stable field kernel
nodes.statement: The additive subgroup generated by s(a,b) is all of K₂(F), for every field F. This is only the field refinement of the predecessor’s semilocal generation target.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: Choose a finite Steinberg word representing a stable kernel element. Its elementary image is identity already at a sufficiently large finite rank, since the finite matrix embeddings are injective.
By complete toral relations, that word is a product of conjugates of toral defects and their inverses.
In stable St each defect is the chosen symbol and is central. Drop the conjugations to obtain a finite sum of symbols.
This argument requires the predecessor’s finite-representative/colimit API and stable centrality, retained as inherited proof obligations. It does not prove generation for arbitrary semilocal rings.
acceptance: Every stable kernel element has a displayed finite sum of symbols.
No claim about finite-rank universality follows from this stable result.

sources.match: Extracts the kernel generators from the complete presentation.
Closes the field branch of the cited generation theorem using the explicit presentation proof.

nodes.title: Torus extension carrying a prescribed symbol
nodes.statement: Given a Steinberg pairing c:Fˣ×Fˣ→A and r=n-1≥2, let H₀=(Fˣ)^r with ordered simple coroots α_i=e_i-e_{i+1}. Put β(s,t)=Σ_i c(s_i,t_i)−Σ_{i>j, i=j+1} c(s_i,t_j). Give H_c=A×H₀ the product (a,s)(b,t)=(a+b+β(s,t),st). It is a central extension of the SL_n diagonal torus by A, with h_i(s)h_i(t)h_i(st)⁻¹=c(s,t) and [h_i(s),h_j(t)]=a_{ji}c(s,t), where a_{ii}=2, adjacent a_{ji}=-1 and all other entries are zero.
hypotheses: F is a field, A is an abelian group, c is a Steinberg pairing, n≥3 and r=n-1.
proofSteps: Each term of β is biadditive in the multiplicative coordinates, so β(s,t)+β(st,u)=β(s,tu)+β(t,u); β at either identity is zero. This gives associativity and identity on the displayed carrier.
The inverse is (-a-β(s,s⁻¹),s⁻¹). Projection onto H₀ is onto; inclusion a↦(a,1) is injective and its image is the kernel and is central.
Compute defects and commutators using the coordinate formula and skew-symmetry. The same-coordinate commutator is 2c(s,t), explaining the diagonal Cartan entry.
Identify H₀ with diagonal matrices of determinant one by s↦diag(s₁,s₁⁻¹s₂,…,s_{r-1}⁻¹s_r,s_r⁻¹). The inverse reads successive products of diagonal entries.
acceptance: The conclusion holds at the displayed maps, with the stated orientations and hypotheses.

nodes.title: Extended Weyl square-subgroup presentation
nodes.statement: For the type-A chain with r=n-1≥2 let W̃ be generated by q_i with adjacent length-three braids, nonadjacent commutation, and q_i²q_jq_i⁻²=q_j^{(-1)^{a_{ji}}}. Its square subgroup D generated by d_i=q_i² has the presentation d_i⁻¹d_jd_i=d_j d_i^{1-(-1)^{a_{ji}}}. In particular q_i⁴ is a common nontrivial central element of order two, and W̃/D is S_n. These are square-subgroup relations, not the relation q_i⁴=1.
hypotheses: n≥3, r=n-1 and the Cartan entries are those of A_r. This theorem is independent of the field.
proofSteps: The defining relations make the fourth powers central; the ordinary signed-Weyl presentation identifies the quotient by them. Collect square words using the displayed conjugation relations. They force d_i⁴=1 and equality of d_i² along the connected type-A chain.

To prove there are no further square relations, realize the candidate D on (ℤ/2)×(ℤ/2)^r with factor set B(x,y)=Σ_i x_i y_i+Σ_{i=j+1} x_i y_j. Its coordinate generators square to the common central coefficient 1 and have precisely the adjacent/nonadjacent commutators. Collection gives at most 2^(r+1) elements, and this model has exactly that size.

Define auxiliary θ_i⁻¹(d_j)=d_j d_i^{b_ij}, where b_ij=(1−(-1)^{a_ij})/2: it is 1 for adjacent distinct vertices and 0 otherwise, including i=j. Thus the auxiliary action fixes d_i. Verify θ_i²=Ad(d_i) and the type-A braids. On D×S_n define Λ_i(t,w)=(θ_i(t),s_iw) when length increases, and Λ_i(t,w)=(θ_i(t d_i),s_iw) when length decreases. Their squares translate by d_i, so D acts faithfully; rank-two braid checks give a representation of W̃ preserving the candidate square group.
This faithful realization proves the displayed square relations exhaustive and the central fourth power nontrivial. Modulo D the Coxeter presentation gives S_n.
acceptance: For r=2 the square subgroup has eight elements, with both generating squares equal to the nontrivial central coefficient.
The proof is a lifted presentation calculation; ordinary Coxeter word invariance is imported.

sources.match: Specializes the auxiliary doubled signed-Weyl group to the connected simply laced type-A chain; the mod-two model spells out the square-subgroup realization.

nodes.title: Lifted monomial extension
nodes.statement: Extend H_c to a central extension N_c of the determinant-one monomial matrix group N₀. Its simple Weyl lifts q_i project to w_{i,i+1}(-1), satisfy q_i²=h_i(-1), commute for nonadjacent i,j and satisfy q_iq_jq_i=q_jq_iq_j for adjacent i,j. Conjugation by q_i acts by θ_i; θ_i⁻¹ fixes A and sends h_j(t) to h_j(t)h_i(t^{-a_{ij}}). The map H_c→N_c is injective; N_c/H_c is the symmetric group S_n.
hypotheses: F is a field, A is abelian, c is a Steinberg pairing and n≥3.
proofSteps: Check that the proposed θ_i⁻¹ images preserve every torus defect and commutator relation using bilinearity, c(t,-t)=0 and the diagonal 2-torsion equation.
Check θ_i²=Ad(h_i(-1)), the adjacent braid relation and the nonadjacent commuting relation. These are explicit type-A computations on the torus generators.

Introduce the auxiliary group W̃ generated by q_i with the braid relations and q_i²q_jq_i⁻²=q_j^{(-1)^{a_{ji}}}. Its square subgroup maps to H_c by q_i²↦h_i(-1), using the proved lifted-weyl-square-presentation; its adjacent commutator and common central squares map correctly by the torus Cartan formula and 2c(-1,-1)=0.
Form H_c⋊W̃ and quotient by the graph subgroup identifying these squares. The graph subgroup is normal and meets H_c trivially; prove this intersection before claiming injectivity.

Using the ordinary Weyl presentation and reduced-word property, collect every element into a torus element times a chosen reduced Weyl lift. Compute the kernel of N_c→N₀ as precisely A. No relation q_i⁴=1 is added: it can erase c(-1,-1).
acceptance: The conclusion holds at the displayed maps, with the stated orientations and hypotheses.

nodes.title: Matsumoto’s permutation construction
nodes.statement: For an infinite field F and prescribed pairing c, let v:SL_n(F)→N₀ be the unique monomial middle component in U⁺NU⁺. Define S_c={(g,m)∈SL_n(F)×N_c | v(g)=p(m)}. Define E_c as the subgroup of permutations of S_c generated by left torus translations, positive-unipotent translations and simple Weyl transformations. The first coordinate of each generator is the corresponding left matrix translation.
hypotheses: F is an infinite field; A is an abelian group; c is a Steinberg pairing; n≥3.
proofSteps: The map v is a function picking the unique middle monomial, not either outer unipotent factor. Establish its equivariance under left U⁺ and the torus and its two-branch change under w_i(-1), as the specialization of ordinary Bruhat to root coordinates.
A torus lift h acts by (g,m)↦(p(h)g,hm); u∈U⁺ acts by (g,m)↦(ug,m).

For q_i the first coordinate is w_i(-1)g. If v(w_i(-1)g)=w_i(-1)v(g), the second coordinate becomes q_i m. Otherwise there is a unique nonzero root parameter t and v(w_i(-1)g)=h_i(t⁻¹)v(g); the second coordinate becomes h_i(t⁻¹)m.
Check membership in S_c and bijectivity of each transformation. The Weyl inverse follows from λ_i²=λ(h_i(-1)), with both branches verified.

A acts faithfully and centrally on the second coordinates. Its orbit set is SL_n(F), so the first-coordinate action defines a surjection E_c→SL_n(F). Exactness of its kernel is the separate theorem below, not assumed in this construction.
acceptance: The conclusion holds at the displayed maps, with the stated orientations and hypotheses.

nodes.title: Rank-one and rank-two action relations
nodes.statement: The root and Weyl transformations in E_c satisfy the type-A Steinberg relations. Each rank-one root subgroup with its torus realizes the prescribed cocycle c. The adjacent simple Weyl transformations satisfy the length-three braid relation, and transformations belonging to disconnected simple roots commute.
hypotheses: F is an infinite field; c is a Steinberg pairing to abelian A; n≥3.
proofSteps: Define inversion on S_c by (g,m)↦(g⁻¹,m⁻¹), and conjugate the left transformation group by it to obtain the right transformation group.

Torus and positive-root left transformations commute with the right generators. Reduce the remaining left/right Weyl commutation to a rank-one or rank-two root subsystem and its minimal Weyl-coset representative.

Use orbit representatives (x_α(u)w(σ)x_β(v), lift(w(σ))) and split the three cases σβ≠±α, σβ=α and σβ=-α. In the last case isolate u=0, v=0 or uv=1; when uv(1-uv)≠0 use c(u⁻¹,(v-u⁻¹)⁻¹)=c((u-v⁻¹)⁻¹,v⁻¹). This follows by bilinearity and the Steinberg relation, and is the essential cocycle cancellation.

Left and right groups are transitive and commute, hence each acts freely: an element fixing one point fixes its orbit under the commuting transitive group. Verify the Weyl braid at (1,1), then use freeness to promote the equality to permutations.
Restrict the rank-one/rank-two checks to each embedded subsystem and transport to arbitrary cosets. Conjugating the simple root generators gives all roots and their Steinberg commutator formulas.
acceptance: The exceptional uv=1 branch is checked without an inverse of zero.
The braid equation is proved as an equality of permutations on the entire fiber set.
A condition asserting these action relations is not added to the input data.

nodes.title: Exact central extension realizing the pairing
nodes.statement: The projection E_c→SL_n(F) has kernel exactly the embedded coefficient group A, and its root lifts have toral defect c. Thus 1→A→E_c→SL_n(F)→1 is a central extension realizing the prescribed pairing, with A included injectively.
hypotheses: F is an infinite field, A is abelian, c is a Steinberg pairing and n≥3.
proofSteps: Embed N_c into E_c using the verified local relations and coefficient/torus translations. Its quotient by the lifted torus is the ordinary Weyl group.

Show E_c is the union of Ũ⁺H̃ w̃ Ũ⁺: the union contains 1 and is stable under left multiplication by its generating transformations. Increasing-length cases move a root past w̃; decreasing-length cases use the verified rank-one decomposition, with its torus inverse parameter.
If an element projects to 1, ordinary Bruhat forces the Weyl component to be 1 and then its torus coordinate to be 1. Unipotent injectivity eliminates the outer factors, leaving precisely A.

The prescribed torus defect is retained under the injective torus embedding. Centrality and injectivity were established in the permutation action, so the identification of the kernel does not erase nonzero coefficients.
acceptance: At c=p with A=P₂(F), inl(p(-1,-1)) remains nonzero over ℝ.
Exactness includes both containment directions and surjectivity.

nodes.title: Finite-field classical kernel vanishing
nodes.statement: For a finite field F, every explicit classical symbol s(a,b) vanishes and the stable classical group K₂(F) is zero. The proof works over F₂, F₃ and F₄ and asserts no finite-rank universal-central-extension statement.
hypotheses: F is a finite field.
proofSteps: By the independently proved abstract finite-field tensor-square vanishing, every Steinberg pairing over F is zero. Apply this to the explicit classical pairing.
The stable kernel is generated by these zero symbols, hence is itself zero. This uses neither infinite-field extension realization nor Matsumoto injectivity.
Alternatively repeat the cyclic generator, diagonal 2-torsion and nonsquare-pair proof directly on the classical pairing; the same F₂ and characteristic-two branches apply.
Keep the result at stable K₂. No finite-rank centrality or universality is deduced from it.
acceptance: K₂(F₂)=K₂(F₃)=K₂(F₄)=0.
Stable vanishing is established before invoking Matsumoto’s all-field equivalence.

nodes.title: Finite-field tensor-square vanishing
nodes.statement: For a finite field F, P₂(F)=0 and Kᴹ₂(F)=0, independently of the classical comparison. Every Steinberg pairing from F to an abelian group is zero.
hypotheses: F is a finite field.
proofSteps: Choose a generator g of Fˣ using cyclicity; in F₂ the sole unit is 1. Multilinearity makes P₂(F) cyclic on p(g,g).
If char F=2, -1=1 and the diagonal identity gives p(g,g)=0.

If char F≠2, 2p(g,g)=0. There are (q−1)/2 nonsquares but only (q−3)/2 nonzero squares other than 1: the squaring map on units has kernel {1,−1} and fibers of size two. If every nonsquare u had 1−u square, the injection u↦1−u would put the larger set into the smaller one (1−u is neither 0 nor 1). Hence choose nonsquares u=g^m,v=g^n with u+v=1. The exponents m,n are odd, so p(u,v)=mn·p(g,g)=p(g,g), but the Steinberg relation makes this zero.
Generation proves the whole quotient vanishes; its universal property makes every pairing zero. Transfer this to the actual Milnor degree-two component through its already proved equivalence.
acceptance: P₂(F₂)=P₂(F₃)=P₂(F₄)=0.
No assertion that every skew pairing on a cyclic group is zero substitutes for the Steinberg relation.

hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: Use the actual diagonal commutator pairing, not an abstract isomorphism chosen from Matsumoto.
Descend it through the tensor-square quotient and compose with the degree-two equivalence in the specified direction.
Every symbol is in the image, so generation proves surjectivity.
Uniqueness on symbols records the exact map for naturality and product comparisons.

nodes.title: Faithful symbols over infinite fields
nodes.statement: For an infinite field F, the map P₂(F)→Additive K₂(F) induced by s is injective. A finite additive combination of symbols that is trivial in stable St already vanishes in P₂(F).
hypotheses: F is an infinite field.
proofSteps: Take A=P₂(F) and c=p, its universal pairing. A putative relation is a finite product of stable symbol words.
If that word is 1 in stable St, the predecessor’s finite-representative equality yields a rank n≥3 where the corresponding St_n word is 1.

At that rank, the verified root lifts in E_p satisfy the Steinberg relations and hence give St_n(F)→E_p via the presented-group universal property. No compatibility between E_p at different ranks is required.
Each chosen symbol maps to inl(p(a,b)) by the positive-root cocycle normalization. The word maps to the coefficient inclusion of the alleged relation.
Since A→E_p is injective, the relation vanishes in A. This proves injectivity for the chosen map rather than for a possibly differently oriented presentation.
acceptance: No stable UCE uniqueness theorem is needed to define the detecting map from St_n.
The proof uses finite-representative equality, not an unsupported injectivity of all St_n→St_{n+1}.

nodes.title: A real symbol detecting the integral diagonal
nodes.statement: Define ε:ℝˣ→ℤ/2 to be 1 on negative units and 0 on positive units. The function c∞(a,b)=ε(a)ε(b) is a Steinberg pairing. It descends to P₂(ℝ)→ℤ/2 and therefore detects the nonzero order-two class {-1,-1} in Milnor and classical K₂(ℝ). It also defines a graded map Kᴹ(ℝ)→(ℤ/2)[t] sending the degree-one class of a to ε(a)t.
hypotheses: F=ℝ and the coefficient target is ℤ/2.
proofSteps: The sign of a product gives ε(ab)=ε(a)+ε(b) in ℤ/2. A unit is never zero, so positivity and negativity cover all inputs.
If a+b=1, the two units cannot both be negative, so their two sign values multiply to zero. This proves the pairing condition without Hilbert symbols or a Brauer-group comparison.
Descend by the universal property. Its value on p(-1,-1) is 1, while the diagonal identity makes twice that class zero.
For the graded detector extend the degree-one linear sign map to the tensor algebra. Its Steinberg products vanish, so it factors through the homogeneous quotient and respects degree.
acceptance: The conclusion holds at the displayed maps, with the stated orientations and hypotheses.

nodes.title: Permutation signs without integral alternation
nodes.statement: In the imported Milnor ring, interchanging adjacent unit entries negates an n-symbol. A permutation π multiplies a symbol by sign(π). A consecutive repeated entry can be replaced by (a,-1); in characteristic two such a consecutive repeat vanishes. The sign rule alone does not make all repeated-entry symbols vanish integrally.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; coefficients in every symbol group are integral.
proofSteps: Apply the abstract degree-two identities to p, then transport to the actual Milnor degree-two piece.
Multiply a degree-two identity on the left and right by the products of the remaining entries; concatenation supplies the adjacent interchange and repeated-entry equations.
Decompose a permutation into adjacent transpositions. Parity makes the resulting sign independent of the decomposition.
The real graded sign map sends {-1,…,-1} to t^n, nonzero in every degree. It supplies a counterexample to any inference that repeated entries always vanish.
acceptance: The degree-two equation is {a,a}={a,-1}, not zero.

Matsumoto Lemma 5.4(c), p. 26 agrees for the +1 root overlap. The discrepancy need not vanish: the t-adic pairing on ℚ(t) sends the (t,2) symbol to 2 (Weibel III.6.3, p. 51), distinct from its inverse.
